title: Australia should tax gas exports rather than reserve gas for domestic buyers
oneLiner: The competing proposal from the Greens and Senator Pocock: price the exports, do not ration them.
body: Instead of requiring producers to set gas aside, an export levy would make overseas sales less attractive relative to domestic ones and return revenue to the public. The Greens argued the reservation policy was written by the industry for the industry; Senator David Pocock's dissenting report to a Senate committee recommended a 25 per cent tax on all gas exports. The government ruled out gas tax increases in the May 2026 budget, citing fuel security during the Middle East conflict.
contextBackground: A competing answer to the same problem, argued at the same Senate committee that considered reservation. It belongs in this debate because the case for reservation is partly the case against doing this instead. Its two factual legs, that a tax would lower prices and that it would raise revenue, are argued separately below.
contextDisagreement: Supporters of reservation say a tax raises exporters' costs without guaranteeing any domestic volume; supporters of a tax say reservation guarantees volume for whoever producers choose to sell to, at a price the government will not forecast, and forgoes the revenue.

evidenceItems.citation: ABC News, 7 May 2026 — Greens and Pocock positions on export taxation; government rules out budget gas tax changes

otherClaim.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices

claimItself.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices
claimItself.oneLiner: Australia has decided to reserve gas for domestic buyers. The question now is whether the scheme, as designed and then softened, will do what it was announced to do.
claimItself.body: In May 2026 the federal government announced that Queensland's three LNG export ventures must reserve a share of export volumes for Australian users from July 2027, with contracts signed before 22 December 2025 exempt. In September 2026 the rule was recast around forecast domestic demand rather than a flat share of exports. The government says prices will fall; it will not say by how much.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Because export contracts signed before 22 December 2025 are exempt, the scheme reaches too little gas to move prices for years

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Mandatory reservation will deter investment in new gas supply and worsen the shortfall it is meant to fix

otherClaim.title: A tax on gas exports would lower domestic gas prices

claimItself.title: A tax on gas exports would lower domestic gas prices
claimItself.oneLiner: The effect claim underneath the tax proposal.
claimItself.body: If exporting attracts a levy and domestic sales do not, producers have a reason to sell locally at a price below export parity, and the domestic price settles lower. Proponents argue this works through price rather than volume, so it does not depend on how much gas a reservation scheme captures or on which contracts are exempt.

strengthDefinitions.decisive: The parent claim largely stands or falls on this one.
strengthDefinitions.relevant: It adds real weight, but the parent claim survives without it.
strengthDefinitions.tangential: True perhaps, but it does little work for this claim.

otherClaim.title: An export tax would raise public revenue that a reservation scheme forgoes

claimItself.title: An export tax would raise public revenue that a reservation scheme forgoes
claimItself.oneLiner: Reservation moves gas; a tax also moves money.
claimItself.body: A levy on exports accrues to the budget; a reservation obligation does not. Senator Pocock's dissent paired a 25 per cent export tax with a cap on decommissioning-cost deductions as a revenue package. A cross-party Senate committee agreed the government should revisit gas taxation once the Middle East conflict ends, without reaching consensus on the design.
